headline: Steady traffic growth drives higher sales and profit
summary_short: Texas Roadhouse grew Q1 2026 revenue 12.8% y/y to $1,633.2M on a 7.1% comp-sales gain, with net income up 8.6% to $123.4M and diluted EPS up 9.6% to $1.87, even as commodity and wage inflation pushed restaurant margin down to 16.3% from 16.6%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 12.8% y/y to $1,633.2M on 7.1% comparable-restaurant-sales growth (higher traffic and average check) plus 5.7% store-week growth from new openings and franchise acquisitions. Restaurant margin dollars grew 10.5% to $264.4M, but margin as a percentage of sales slipped to 16.3% from 16.6% on 6.2% commodity inflation and 3.8% wage inflation, partly offset by higher sales. Net income rose 8.6% to $123.4M and diluted EPS rose 9.6% to $1.87, helped by buybacks. Q1 capital allocation: $80.2M capex, $71.8M franchise acquisitions, $49.4M dividends, $28.2M buybacks, plus a $50M draw on the revolver. For FY2026, management guides to 5-6% store-week growth, 6-7% commodity inflation, 3-4% wage inflation, ~$400M capex, and a 14-15% effective tax rate.

drivers.explanation: Comp-sales and store-week growth lifted revenue and profit; commodity and wage inflation compressed restaurant margin percentage, but higher margin dollars and buybacks still grew net income and EPS.
Driven by 7.1% comparable-restaurant-sales growth (higher guest traffic and per-person average check) and 5.7% store-week growth from new openings and franchise acquisitions.
Higher restaurant margin dollars drove the gain, partially offset by higher depreciation and amortization and higher general and administrative expenses.
Increase reflects the rise in net income plus the reduced share count from ongoing share repurchases.
Decline was primarily due to commodity inflation of 6.2% and wage and other labor inflation of 3.8%, partially offset by higher sales.
Increase reflects a $50.0 million draw on the revolving credit facility entered into in April 2025, up from zero outstanding last quarter.
Share count fell y/y as the company continued repurchasing stock ($28.2M in Q1 2026) under its $500M buyback program.
